summary: Four silent deaths were not diagnosed because the launcher discarded the evidence, not because the failure was opaque.
detail: setsid nohup ... > log 2>&1 & threw away the exit status (139/134/137 would have named the cause), block-buffered stdout so up to 8KB of startup output was lost at signal death, and ran without PYTHONFAULTHANDLER so a native crash produced no stack. The 0-byte train4.log was read as 'wrote nothing'; it only ever meant 'died before filling one 8KB buffer'.
resolution: experiments/v0_smoke/launch.sh added: exit code recorded, PYTHONFAULTHANDLER + PYTHONUNBUFFERED, signal names, dmesg capture.

summary: verifiers kills the oolong env worker every 30s; no rollout can ever complete.
detail: env_server.log: 'EnvRouter - WARNING - Worker 0 heartbeat timeout (32.8s), restarting'. worker_heartbeat_timeout defaults to 30.0s in verifiers/serve/server/env_{server,router}.py. Building a 32768-65536 token oolong context takes longer than that, so the router executes its own worker roughly every 66s in an unbounded loop. 'Active tasks: 0' throughout; 3 completion requests reached vLLM in 13 minutes and both GPUs sat at 0% while CPU workers churned. Not exposed through smoke.toml.
resolution: Raised worker_heartbeat_timeout 30.0 -> 900.0 on the pod and relaunched. Needs a proper home: either a prime-rl env config field or a smaller min_ctx/max_ctx for the smoke test.

summary: oolong returns raw dicts from prompt_messages, forcing repeated normalize_messages.
detail: env_worker_0.log: 'prompt_messages returned raw dicts/strings instead of vf.Messages. This repeatedly triggers normalize_messages'. Emitted once per worker start. It makes context construction slower, which is the exact step that blows the 30s heartbeat, so the two defects compound.
resolution: Fix in the sid19arya/rlm fork: return vf.Messages from prompt_messages in the oolong environment.

summary: pkill -9 -f vllm matched my own ssh command string and killed the session.
detail: The remote command contained the word 'vllm', so pkill matched the ssh-spawned shell running it. The relaunch never fired and orphaned processes kept 36GB+16GB of GPU memory. Kill by PID from nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps instead of by pattern.

summary: Trainer OOMs in the backward pass at step 1; activation checkpointing was never configured.
detail: torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 186.00 MiB. GPU has 44.43 GiB capacity, 176.62 MiB free. Failure is in the QKV projection (Linear 4096->12288), i.e. stored activations, not weights -- Qwen3-8B bf16 is ~16GB and LoRA adds only 30M trainable params. smoke.toml set no [trainer.model.ac] block, so nothing was recomputed. Would OOM identically on a 48GB A40.
resolution: Added [trainer.model.ac] mode='full' freq=1 to smoke.toml. Costs ~30% step time.

summary: The OOM lands one step AFTER its cause, because step 0 only collects rollouts.
detail: Step 0 completed successfully in 420.66s -- it gathers rollouts and trains only at the step boundary. The trainer OOM therefore surfaced during step 1, which read as 'step 1 is slow' for 14 minutes before I looked at trainer.log and found the process had died at 18:03. A step that appears to run long may be a crashed trainer, not a slow one: check GPU utilisation and trainer.log before assuming progress.

summary: Repeated the pkill self-match bug I had already documented an hour earlier.
detail: pkill -9 -f 'root/launch.sh' matched the ssh-spawned shell running that very command, killing the session before the relaunch fired. Identical to the earlier 'pkill -9 -f vllm' incident, which is already recorded in this file. Writing the lesson down did not stop me repeating it; the fix is to never pattern-kill from a command whose own text contains the pattern -- kill by PID.

summary: Trainer peak memory climbs step over step: 40.95 -> 43.43 GB of 44.43 GiB.
detail: perf/peak_memory across steps 0-4: 40.95, 40.95, 42.14, 43.43, 43.43. ~1GB headroom left on a 48GB A6000. Activation checkpointing bought room but something still accumulates per step, so the run may OOM again around step 10-15 -- the same failure as run 7, delayed rather than fixed. Needs a cause before any 250-step commitment.
resolution: Unresolved. Watch peak_memory to step 10; if it has not plateaued, this config does not survive a long run on 48GB at any budget.

detail: W&B effective_batch_size/all per step: 0.5, 0.5, 1, nan, 1, 0.5, 1. Combined with the persistent 'Detected 4/8 rollouts (zero_advantage=4), enforced 4', each step trains on roughly ONE usable sample. errored_rollouts and empty_rollouts are both 0, so this is the advantage filter and grouping, not rollout failure. Sample efficiency this low makes the reward series uninterpretable and would make a 250-step run costly for very little signal.
resolution: Open question for V1: raise rollouts per step, or revisit the zero_advantage filter, before scaling.

summary: Step-time growth is on the rollout side, not the trainer.
detail: Step times 277/204/287/369/369/483s climb ~50s/step, but perf/throughput holds at 1500-1800 tok/s and perf/mfu at ~22% across the same steps. The trainer is not degrading, so the growth is in rollout generation on the inference GPU -- consistent with vLLM KV-cache or prefix accumulation. perf/ metrics do not cover the inference side, which is why the trend is invisible from the trainer's own numbers.
resolution: Instrument the inference side before V1; the trainer metrics alone would have hidden this.
